metric_rationale: In this experimental design, the trials can be divided into 'compensatory' (where the single best cue points to one option, but the sum of the remaining cues points to the other) and 'non-compensatory' (where the best cue and the sum of cues agree). This metric computes the difference in the rate of Take-The-Best (TTB) consistent choices between non-compensatory and compensatory trials. For the TTB model, this difference will be near zero because it uses the same one-reason strategy on both trial types. For the Weighted Additive (WADD) model, the difference will be significantly greater than zero because it frequently chooses the opposite of TTB on compensatory trials while agreeing with TTB on non-compensatory trials.

The experimental design is carefully constructed such that for every trial, the single most valid discriminating cue predicts one option (which Take The Best will choose), while the sum of the remaining discriminating cues predicts the other option (which Weighted Additive will choose). By measuring the proportion of trials where the subject's response aligns with the TTB prediction, we obtain a metric that will be very high (~1.0) under TTB and very low (~0.0) under WADD.
